_comment: The approved workspace-retrieval branch, closed. This file is the switch:
there is no environment variable, no Settings field and no operator toggle
that turns semantic workspace recall on, because the evidence is what turns
it on. Runtime configuration cannot be more permissive than this artifact —
it cannot be more permissive at all, having no say in the matter.
Read at import time by contextplane/context/semantic_workspace.py, which
refuses to load a branch outside the frozen table and refuses on any digest
file to widen the arm therefore does not widen the arm; it stops the process.
Any change here is a change to a recorded decision and belongs to whoever
owns that decision, not to whoever is changing the code that reads it.

decision.authority: operator-ratified adjudication of the pre-registered campaign; the adjudication and the result reading are recorded outside this repository, and everything this file needs a reader to know is written out below rather than cited.

judges.note: Three independent judges split. The decision follows the third with the second's disclosure conditions folded in; the split is part of the record and is not resolved away.

_comment: Narrow by construction, and the narrowness is the approval. The authorized
checkpoint set is resolved first and the scan sees nothing else, so no
unauthorized item is ever scored, counted, ranked or timed. Broad ANN was
not measured and is not approved; there is no widening path in the code and
no fallback to a larger corpus when the scan finds too few matches, because
'too few authorized matches' is a correct answer.

safety_gates.detail: At floor and within every scenario ceiling in both treatments.

Cross-tenant no-harm is UNMEASURED by this campaign. The tenant term of the safety rubric returned no information, in either direction, and this is not a statement that the system passed it. The scorer read a `tenant_id` key off each served payload; no payload builder in the product has ever emitted that key. The check was a constant function of the system under test — it would have reported a violation for every served item under every possible behaviour, including correct behaviour. And even a correctly implemented check could not have discriminated here: the frozen corpus contains exactly one tenant, every scenario permits exactly that tenant, and the world fixture seeds only that tenant, so no cross-tenant item existed to be leaked. Cross-tenant isolation for workspace recall therefore rests on separate evidence — the tenant predicates in the workspace recall queries and their unit coverage — and not on this campaign. Any downstream artifact that cites this result as evidence of cross-tenant isolation is citing it wrongly.
1.000 in both treatments; served is a subset of relevant.

open_review_obligations.detail: The human risk sample was recorded at collection and has not been reviewed by a human. This branch rests in part on unreviewed safety findings, which is permitted only if the record says so. It says so here. A reviewer who later reads the sample and finds a safety concern invalidates the safety half of this branch.
